articles.title: 4 of family dead: How dispute over hotel lease escalated into mass shooting in Guwahati
articles.description: A deadly shooting occurred at Hotel Bilas Inn in Guwahati, leaving five people dead and one injured. The accused, Ghanakanta Gogoi, had a dispute over the hotel's lease agreement and opened fire. Police arrested him shortly after the incident, seizing a licensed weapon believed to be used in the shooting. Four of the victims were from the same family, highlighting the tragedy of the situation.

Fake seizures, attack on prison guards: How 17 inmates escaped TN jail at midnight
articles.description: Seventeen undertrial inmates managed to escape from Thekkampatti sub-jail in Tamil Nadu's Theni district. They faked epileptic seizures to lure prison personnel into opening their cell. Once the guards entered, the inmates attacked them and fled the facility. Four of the escapees have been apprehended while thirteen remain at large despite extensive police efforts. Investigations into the jailbreak and security lapses at the jail are currently ongoing.

articles.title: Son of AAP sarpanch shot dead outside gurdwara in Amritsar
articles.description: Teerath Singh was shot dead outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village while his friend sustained injuries. Both men were returning from paying respects at the gurdwara when the suspected assailants opened fire. Preliminary investigations indicate the murder was connected to an old land dispute rather than political rivalry. Police have identified four suspects and filed an FIR, but no arrests have been made yet.

Ocean Mixing Barrier Shown: Dye experiment maps slow downward transport; layered structure limits exchange
articles.description: In a recent experiment near Martha’s Vineyard, scientists introduced rhodamine dye into the Atlantic Ocean to study its behavior. The dye spread quickly in the surface waters but demonstrated a slower descent into deeper layers. Findings showed a marked difference in mixing rates, emphasizing the complexities of ocean stratification on substance movement. This research is vital for the advancement of nutrient and pollutant transport models.

Michigan woman buys 128-year-old abandoned church for $45,000 and turns it into her dream home
articles.description: Whitney Anderson, 45, bought a 128-year-old abandoned church in Michigan for $45,000 and is turning it into her dream home. She has spent an estimated $194,000 on renovations since June 2024 and hopes to complete most of the work by 2028. As costs could reach $400,000, Anderson describes the project as the biggest gamble of her life.

articles.title: Oil prices dip on Iran peace hopes, but Saudi attacks keep Brent near six-month highs
articles.description: Oil prices have seen a decline amid diplomatic dialogues aimed at easing Middle Eastern tensions. A meeting between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan, and Iranian officials focused on achieving peace and stability. However, worries linger over the safety of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, due to escalating attacks on commercial vessels. Additionally, Russian refiners are set to ramp up diesel production thanks to a new supply deal with the U.S.

articles.title: UGC NET December 2026 registration closes tomorrow: Over 5.5 lakh candidates registered, check application status
articles.description: UGC NET December 2026: UGC NET December 2026 applications close on October 28, with more than 5.5 lakh candidates registered as of October 25. Of these, 3,73,419 have completed their applications and paid the fee. Another 1,36,993 candidates have yet to upload photographs and signatures or pay the fee, while 31,580 have completed document uploads but still owe payment. Candidates should finish pending formalities and download their confirmation pages. A late-fee application window is scheduled until October 31.

articles.title: HPSOS exam 2027: Check PCP class dates, attendance rules and study centre fee deadline
articles.description: HPSOS March 2027 exams: The Himachal Pradesh State Open School (HPSOS) has made Personal Contact Programme (PCP) class attendance mandatory for fresh admission and additional subject candidates appearing in the March 2027 examinations. Classes will run from February 1 to February 18, 2027, and study centres must submit attendance reports by February 19. Candidates who miss the required classes may not receive admit cards. Private study centres must pay renewal fees by March 31, 2027, or their examination results may be withheld.
